questions.prompt: The Anglo-Zanzibar War is noted chiefly for what distinction?
questions.fact: Fighting is generally recorded as lasting under forty-five minutes, making it the shortest war on record.

questions.prompt: Which structure in the human eye focuses light onto the retina?
questions.fact: It changes shape rather than moving, a mechanism that stiffens with age and causes long-sightedness.

questions.prompt: The Winter Olympics event of skeleton is raced in what position?
questions.fact: Riders reach speeds over 120 kilometres per hour with their chin only centimetres above the ice.

questions.prompt: Which animated sitcom features a scientist and his grandson travelling between dimensions?
questions.fact: It grew out of a crude animated short parodying a well-known time-travel film.

questions.prompt: Which country's territory includes the northernmost permanently inhabited settlements?
questions.fact: Alert, on Ellesmere Island, lies roughly eight hundred kilometres from the North Pole.

questions.prompt: Which Russian author wrote the play The Cherry Orchard?
questions.fact: He called it a comedy; its first director staged it as a tragedy, and the argument has never quite been settled.

questions.prompt: Which storage technology has no moving parts and uses flash memory?
questions.fact: Each cell tolerates a limited number of writes, so controllers spread wear evenly across the whole device.
